timecoded_text_to_speech.text: I was born and raised in Atlanta. I grew up in the sixth district in North of
Cape County, in fact about a half mile from here. Just north of here I'm
Brad Cliff on Hawthorne Drive and I attended Georgetown University's School of
Foreign Service. I worked on Capitol Hill in Washington for five years. Most of
that time for Congressman Hank Johnson staffing his armed services committee
assignment. So I specialized in defense and national security policy and grew
a lot, learned a lot, got to help draft legislation that was passed by Congress
and signed by the president got to work on some sensitive national security
programs and saw what Washington can be at its best and also what Washington is
at its worst. When where do you stand on replacing the affordable care act? I will
be a staunch supporter of maintaining all of the consumer protections that it
affords and making sure that 30 million people are not thrown off of health
insurance roles. I will be a staunch supporter of ensuring that people who have
preexisting conditions do not face price discrimination of inability to get
care that women do not face price discrimination that young people can stay on
the family plan. I've got five years of experience as a national security
staffer in the U.S. Congress. I held a top-secret security clearance. I embarked
with the U.S. Navy on multinational military exercise. I worked on classified
counterterrorism programs and I'm a small business owner who specializes in
anti-corruption investigations. That background I think will allow me to reach
out across the aisle to people who are concerned with national security and
small business issues in a credible way and make the case that I will be well
informed about the issues that they care about and a competent representative of
their concerns as well.
This is our first opportunity to make a statement about what we stand for and
it's our first opportunity to prove that Americans know we can be strong and
prosperous and secure without sacrificing our core values without closing off
to the rest of the world without becoming divided amongst ourselves without
succumbing to meanness and fear and not just that we can be strong and secure and
prosperous without sacrificing those values. Actually we can't remain strong and
secure and prosperous unless we hold true to those values. I think that's what
is at risk here. Thank you so much.

youtube_description:
At a recent meet-and-greet, progressive Congressional candidate Jon Ossoff talked about his professional background, where he stands on the Affordable Care Act and national security, how he plans to reach out to Republicans and the importance of the Congressional District 6 special election on April 18.
